title: Buddhism arrives from Baekje
description: The king of Baekje sends a Buddhist image and scriptures to the Yamato court; the sources disagree on the year.

title: Seventeen-article constitution
description: A set of moral and political precepts for officials is issued, attributed to Prince Shōtoku.

title: Taika Reform
description: After the overthrow of the Soga clan the court begins reforms modelled on Tang China that strengthen the emperor's government.

title: Battle of Baekgang
description: Tang and Silla forces destroy a Japanese fleet sent to restore Baekje, ending Japanese intervention in Korea for centuries.

title: Capital established at Heijō-kyō
description: The first long-lived capital, laid out on the model of Tang Chang'an; start of the Nara period.

title: Capital moved to Heian-kyō
description: Emperor Kanmu moves the court to what becomes Kyoto, the imperial capital for over a thousand years.

title: The Tale of Genji
description: The court lady Murasaki Shikibu writes a long prose romance often called the world's first novel.

title: Battle of Dan-no-ura
description: The Minamoto destroy the Taira fleet, ending the Genpei War.

title: Kamakura shogunate
description: Minamoto no Yoritomo is appointed shogun; warrior government begins.

title: Mongol invasions repelled
description: Two invasion fleets sent by Kublai Khan fail on the coast of Kyushu.

title: Fall of the Kamakura shogunate
description: Forces loyal to Emperor Go-Daigo take Kamakura and the Hōjō regents kill themselves.

title: Ashikaga shogunate founded
description: Ashikaga Takauji drives Go-Daigo from Kyoto and sets up a military government that lasts, at least in name, until 1573.

title: Ōnin War
description: A succession dispute devastates Kyoto and opens the Warring States period.

title: Firearms arrive at Tanegashima
description: Portuguese traders bring matchlock guns, the first recorded European contact with Japan.

title: Francis Xavier lands at Kagoshima
description: The Jesuit missionary brings Christianity to Japan.

title: Battle of Okehazama
description: Oda Nobunaga surprises and kills Imagawa Yoshimoto, whose army was far larger, beginning his rise.

title: Nobunaga enters Kyoto
description: Oda Nobunaga occupies the capital and installs Ashikaga Yoshiaki as shogun, the start of the reunification of Japan.

title: Honnō-ji Incident
description: Akechi Mitsuhide turns on Nobunaga, who dies in the burning temple; Toyotomi Hideyoshi avenges him and takes his place.

title: Siege of Odawara
description: Hideyoshi defeats the Hōjō clan, completing the unification of Japan.

title: Battle of Sekigahara
description: Tokugawa Ieyasu defeats his rivals and becomes master of Japan.

title: Tokugawa shogunate
description: Ieyasu is appointed shogun and governs from Edo; over 250 years of Tokugawa rule follow.

title: Siege of Osaka ends
description: The Tokugawa destroy the Toyotomi family, removing the last rival to their rule.

title: Shimabara Rebellion
description: A rising of peasants, many of them Christian, is crushed, and the shogunate tightens its ban on Christianity.

title: Portuguese ships banned
description: The shogunate expels the Portuguese, leaving the Dutch and Chinese at Nagasaki as Japan's only regular trade with the outside for two centuries.

title: Great Fire of Meireki
description: A fire destroys most of Edo and is estimated to have killed over 100,000 people.

title: Hōei eruption of Mount Fuji
description: Fuji's last eruption covers Edo in ash.

title: Perry arrives at Uraga
description: American warships demand that Japan open to trade, ending two centuries of seclusion.

title: Convention of Kanagawa
description: On Perry's return the shogunate opens two ports to American ships, ending the policy of seclusion.

title: Meiji Restoration
description: Imperial rule is declared restored and the shogunate abolished.

title: Battle of Shiroyama
description: The new conscript army defeats Saigō Takamori's last samurai, ending the Satsuma Rebellion.

title: Meiji Constitution
description: The emperor grants a constitution with an elected lower house, the first in Asia to last.

title: First Sino-Japanese War begins
description: Japanese ships attack a Chinese convoy off Korea; Japan's victory the next year makes it the leading power in East Asia.

title: Battle of Tsushima
description: The Japanese navy destroys the Russian Baltic Fleet, deciding the Russo-Japanese War.

title: Great Kantō earthquake
description: An earthquake and the fires after it destroy much of Tokyo and Yokohama.

title: Mukden Incident
description: Japanese officers blow up a stretch of railway as a pretext for seizing Manchuria.

title: February 26 Incident
description: Young army officers kill several ministers in an attempted coup; its failure leaves the army leadership stronger in politics.

title: Attack on Pearl Harbor
description: Japan attacks the US Pacific Fleet, bringing the United States into the Second World War.

title: Battle of Midway
description: The United States Navy sinks four Japanese aircraft carriers, the turning point of the Pacific War.

title: Atomic bombing of Hiroshima
description: The first use of a nuclear weapon in war; Nagasaki follows three days later.

title: Surrender signed
description: Japan signs the instrument of surrender, ending the Second World War.

title: Firebombing of Tokyo
description: An American incendiary raid burns out much of eastern Tokyo and kills more than 90,000 people in one night.

title: Battle of Okinawa
description: American forces land on Okinawa; three months of fighting kill tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians.

title: Atomic bombing of Nagasaki
description: Three days after Hiroshima a second atomic bomb destroys much of Nagasaki.

title: Emperor announces the surrender
description: Hirohito tells the nation by radio that Japan has accepted the Allied terms.

title: Postwar constitution takes effect
description: The new constitution makes the emperor a symbol of the state and renounces war.

title: Treaty of San Francisco
description: Japan signs a peace treaty with 48 nations, and the occupation ends the following April.

title: Tokyo Olympics
description: The first Olympic Games held in Asia, seen as marking Japan's postwar recovery.

title: Okinawa returned to Japan
description: The United States hands back the Ryukyu Islands after 27 years of administration.

title: Stock market peaks
description: The Nikkei index reaches its high point; the collapse of share and land prices that follows begins decades of slow growth.

title: Kobe earthquake
description: The Great Hanshin earthquake kills more than 6,000 people.

title: Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami
description: A magnitude 9 earthquake and the tsunami it raises kill nearly 20,000 people and cause the Fukushima nuclear accident.
